title: ErrorLLM: Modeling SQL Errors for Text-to-SQL Refinement

problem.claim: Correctly producing SQL queries remains challenging during initial text-to-SQL generation.

gap.claim: Existing self-debugging and self-correction paradigms are limited by ineffective error signals, low detection precision, and hallucination that can corrupt correct SQL queries.

contributions.claim: ErrorLLM explicitly models text-to-SQL errors within a dedicated LLM for SQL refinement.

The framework represents questions and schemas as structural features, uses static detection for execution failures and surface mismatches, and models categorized implicit semantic errors with dedicated error tokens.
Error-guided refinement uses detected errors to guide prompting for SQL-structure refinement.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that ErrorLLM achieves significant improvements over backbone initial generation in extensive experiments.
The authors report that detection quality directly determines refinement effectiveness and that ErrorLLM achieves this through a high detection F1 score.
The corresponding code is released for further research.

narrative_sequence.summary: Initial text-to-SQL generation can produce incorrect SQL queries.
SQL refinement addresses syntactic and semantic errors, but existing self-debugging and self-correction methods have important limitations.
ErrorLLM models errors using structural representations, static detection, categorized error tokens, and error-guided refinement.
The authors report improvements over backbone initial generation and associate refinement effectiveness with detection quality and F1 score.
The corresponding code is released for further research.

source_observation.claim: The framework uses explicit error modeling with structural representations and dedicated error tokens.

interpretation.claim: Making implicit error categories explicit may improve a model's ability to detect complex errors.

application.claim: For structured generation refinement, represent task context and error types explicitly before applying corrective generation.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether this strategy generalizes beyond the reported text-to-SQL setting.

source_observation.claim: The authors report that detection quality directly determines refinement effectiveness.

interpretation.claim: Error detection may be a bottleneck for downstream refinement quality.

application.claim: Evaluate and improve error detection as a separate component in refinement pipelines.

exception.claim: The abstract does not provide the experimental conditions or independent verification needed to assess the strength of this relationship.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify datasets, baselines, quantitative improvement values, or experimental conditions.
The abstract does not detail the training strategy, error categories, or static detection procedure.
The abstract does not provide independent verification of the reported results.
